key_insight: Critically damped Polyak (CDP) stepsizes steer gradient descent toward flatter minima while providing uniform-in-time guarantees for sharpness and loss reduction under locally quadratic assumptions.
engineering_relevance: CDP offers a curvature-adaptive stepsize rule for seeking flatter interpolating solutions, with empirical results extending to pretrained LLM fine-tuning.
method: Multiply the classical Polyak stepsize by 4 and a mild damping factor.
Use critical oscillations near the minimizer manifold while damping drives convergence.
At low loss, induce motion along the manifold that approximately reduces log maximum Hessian eigenvalue.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical guarantees for nonnegative losses with local Morse–Bott structure and empirical flattening similar to SAM in nonlinear teacher–student networks and LLM fine-tuning.
watch_item: The guarantees rely on local geometric assumptions; the reported flattening in broader neural-network settings is empirical rather than covered by the theory.
paper_title: A new algorithmic approach for finding flat minima: critically damped Polyak stepsizes
